definitions.page_found: a TennisLive match page answered HTTP 200 for the match
definitions.with_points: the page lists at least one point state
definitions.complete: games per set equal the final score's (verify_scrape.completeness: exact, a retirement's unfinished game listed, or a match tiebreak as one game)
definitions.only_set_closing_missing: short, and every missing game is the one that closed its set
definitions.other_shortfall: short in some other way (or longer than the score)
definitions.all_points_complete: complete, and no listed game lacks its points
definitions.games_with_points_share: games listed with their points / games in the final score, per record (share_games_with_points_90: records at 90% or more, over all checked)
definitions.with_statistics: the page carries the match statistics block (8 match-level rows on every page seen)
definitions.box_score_check: the statistics block as a box score (aces, double faults, serve points, first serves in, first- and second-serve points won, break points faced and saved; both players) against the reference row's box score; 'players_swapped': the two players' values are exactly exchanged
definitions.winner_agrees: the page's winner is the reference winner
definitions.score_agrees_with_reference: the page's final score has the reference score's games per set

notes_on_intervals: Wilson 95% intervals treat the checked matches as independent draws. They are not: matches come in clusters of 2-4 per drawn edition, and coverage tends to be shared by a tournament's matches, so the intervals are too narrow; 'editions' shows how the outcome falls by edition. 'weighted_to_gap' weights each stratum by its number of gap matches (sample_editions.csv), which the raw shares do not.
exploration: The ledger's first six requests (29 Sep 2026, 17:41-17:45 UTC) were made by hand before the probe ran: a player page (/atp/nicolae-frunza/), the site scripts /Frontend/assets/js/shell.js and app.js (to read how the search box calls /api/search), one /api/player-matches call that reused the token of a page fetched in an earlier Python session and was refused with HTTP 403 (no Cloudflare challenge; the adapter always reads the token from a page fetched in the same session), then the player page and the same API call in one session, which answered 200. The 403 is counted as a session-token error, not a block.
